messages.author: 52e40bac65884605
messages.subject: Including missing with DWLS
parts:
Hello,

I am creating a second order model with SEM with three categorical variable measures repeated on three occasions. I have already run the second order latent variable model and by default it restricts the sample to those with complete information across all occasions (n=7032).

I would like to running it on a sample that has any of the 3 measurement occasions that I think will boost the sample size to approx. 10 000 (rather than complete cases).

My plan is to create a data-frame that provides me with the sample I'm interested in (any of 3 measurement occasions, approx. n=10 000) and then run it on that.


I'm looking for syntax that would include not just the 7032 complete cases, but those with missing as well.

However, as I'm using the DWLS estimator I cannot find a way/syntax to include missing data, such that it doesn't only run on complete cases.

I have tried the following syntax to retain all available data with DWLS but I get this error messages. 

 secondordermodelmml <- '
Attachmentat18 =~ rkd420 + rkd421 + rkd422
Attachmentat30 =~ rkf394 + rkf392 + r_rkf393
Attachmentat42 =~ rkj333 + r_rkj331 + r_rkj332
Attachment =~ Attachmentat42 + Attachmentat18 + Attachmentat30'

secondorderfitmml <- sem(secondordermodelmml, data=cleandata) 
summary(secondorderfitmml,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE, estimator="mml", missing="fiml")
Error in .local(object, ...) : 
  unused arguments (estimator = "mml", missing = "fiml")


secondordermodelmml <- '
Attachmentat18 =~ rkd420 + rkd421 + rkd422
Attachmentat30 =~ rkf394 + rkf392 + r_rkf393
Attachmentat42 =~ rkj333 + r_rkj331 + r_rkj332
Attachment =~ Attachmentat42 + Attachmentat18 + Attachmentat30'

secondorderfitmml <- sem(secondordermodelmml, data=cleandata) 
summary(secondorderfitmml,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE, estimator="mml", missing="pairwise")
Error in .local(object, ...) : 
 unused arguments (estimator = "mml", missing = "pairwise")


secondordermodelmml <- '
Attachmentat18 =~ rkd420 + rkd421 + rkd422
Attachmentat30 =~ rkf394 + rkf392 + r_rkf393
Attachmentat42 =~ rkj333 + r_rkj331 + r_rkj332
Attachment =~ Attachmentat42 + Attachmentat18 + Attachmentat30'
secondorderfitmml <- sem(secondordermodelmml, data=cleandata) 
summary(secondorderfitmml,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE, missing="pairwise")
Error in .local(object, ...) : unused argument (missing = "pairwise")

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Including missing with DWLS
parts:
You're putting missing="pairwise" in the wrong place. It goes in the sem() call, not the summary() call.

Same goes for estimator="mml"

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Including missing with DWLS
parts:
For the first question, yes, missing="pairwise" is usually the best option for DWLS. It's using all measures. It analyzes the polychoric correlation matrix, where each correlation coefficient in the matrix is based on all respondents who provided data to both variables going into that coefficient. This set of respondents may vary coefficient to coefficient, which can lead to estimation problems if you have a lot of missing.

Reasons to choose DWLS vs MML I'll leave to those better qualified.

Pat

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Including missing with DWLS
parts: What is the difference between using missing="pairwise" with DWLS

This is a limited-information technique, and it assumes MCAR (restrictive, unrealistic).  For each pair of variables, it estimates their polychoric correlation using all available cases that provided data on both of those variables.
vs. estimator="mml" and missing="fiml"?

This is a full-information technique, and it assumes MAR (less restrictive, realistic if your model includes variables related to missingness).  It is preferable in principle, but MML is very computationally intensive (requires numerical integration over the latent dimensions), so it may not be feasible for models with more than 2-3 latent variables.  Try running a single-factor CFA in lavaan to see how long that runs, then a 2-factor CFA and notice already how much that will increase the run time.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
